To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a chromosome 1 region affecting blood pressure and vascular disease traits was isolated in the stroke-prine spontaneously hypertensive rat model.

a region on chromosome 1 of the SHRSP/Izumo strain affects both BP and stroke, and that the same region affects glucose tolerance, and that these traits can be separated in the F2 progeny of SHR/Izumo.
a chromosomal region on rat chromosome 2 is responsible for blood pressure and associated vascular disease traits in a rat strain with spontaneous hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic dissection of complex traits, and we are currently working on the positional cloning of this locus.
the identification of genetic determinants underlying complex phenotypes in a rat model of stroke.
the genetic dissection of hypertension, stroke, and diabetes mellitus, and the results obtained are expected to provide new insights into the pathogenesis of these diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a single QTL is responsible for BP and vascular disease traits in SHRSP/Izumino.
the RNO1 region affects BP, stroke, impaired glucose tolerance, and vascular disease in the SHRSP model.
RNO1 is a major QTL affecting BP, but not stroke, in SHRSP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QTL on RNO1 is not directly related to stroke but may be a common factor for hypertension and stroke, as well as for hypertension and diabetes.

a QTL for BP is located on rat chromosome 6, and that a QTL affecting stroke is present on rat chromosome 10 in the Izm colony, but that these two QTL are distinct from each other and from those reported previously for BP and/or stroke in the Heidelberg colony.
a major QTL for BP on RNO1 is a common genetic factor for stroke and impaired glucose tolerance in SHR/Izm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single gene on RNO1 may contribute to BP, stroke, or glucose intolerance in the SHRSP/Izn model.
a single gene can affect several phenotypic traits in the same organism.
the genetic background is important in defining the phenotypic outcome of a given genetic locus, and that the genetic background may be different for different phenotypes.
